title: The pressure of ministry
scripture_text: “I am sending you out like sheep among wolves. Therefore be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves. Be on your guard; you will be handed over to the local councils and be flogged in the synagogues. On my account you will be brought before governors and kings as witnesses to them and to the Gentiles. But when they arrest you, do not worry about what to say or how to say it. At that time you will be given what to say, for it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you “Brother will betray brother to death, and a father his child; children will rebel against their parents and have them put to death. You will be hated by everyone because of me, but the one who stands firm to the end will be saved. When you are persecuted in one place, flee to another. Truly I tell you, you will not finish going through the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes. The student is not above the teacher, nor a servant above his master. It is enough for students to be like their teachers, and servants like their masters. If the head of the house has been called Beelzebul, how much more the members of his household! So do not be afraid of them, for there is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, or hidden that will not be made known. What I tell you in the dark, speak in the daylight; what is whispered in your ear, proclaim from the roofs. Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Rather, be afraid of the One who can destroy both soul and body in hell. Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? Yet not one of them will fall to the ground outside your Father’s care. And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. So don’t be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows. “Whoever acknowledges me before others, I will also acknowledge before my Father in heaven. But whoever disowns me before others, I will disown before my Father in heaven. Do not suppose that I have come to bring peace to the earth. I did not come to bring peace, but a sword. For I have come to turn a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law—a man’s enemies will be the members of his own household. Anyone who loves their father or mother more than me is not worthy of me; anyone who loves their son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me. Whoever does not take up their cross and follow me is not worthy of me. Whoever finds their life will lose it, and whoever loses their life for my sake will find it. Anyone who welcomes you welcomes me, and anyone who welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me. Whoever welcomes a prophet as a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward, and whoever welcomes a righteous person as a righteous person will receive a righteous person’s reward. And if anyone gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones who is my disciple, truly I tell you, that person will certainly not lose their reward.”
devotional:
Knowledge of God being your Father is essential if we are going to cope with the pressure of ministry. Jesus refers to ’the Spirit of your Father.’ Matthew 10:20. This is the only time we come across this phrase in the bible, but what I think Jesus is saying here, is that life in the Spirit is never separated from intimacy with God our Father, and dependence on God as our father. Intimacy and dependence are essential if we are going to respond spiritually to pressure.

All our witnessing should be an expression of freedom.

If we are not free outside the court, then we won’t be free inside the court.

Often difficulties and pressure reveal what kind of relationship we have the God our Father, and with the Holy Spirit.

We will need to learn how to cope with hostile relationships if we are going to respond properly to the pressure of ministry.

In verses 21-23 the conflict deepens and becomes more personal. It is much easier to be persecuted by local authorities or courts, than it is to be persecuted by family and people we know and love.

Jesus says: -

"Brother will betray brother to death, and a father his child; children will rebel against their parents and have them put to death. All men will hate you because of me, but he who stands firm to the end will be saved. When you are persecuted in one place, flee to another. I tell you the truth, you will not finish going through the cities of Israel before the Son of Man comes.’’

A true indication of how spiritual we are, will be seen in how we handle relationships, be they good or bad. In these verses Jesus is telling his disciples that they are going to face difficult relationships, and how they respond to those difficult painful relationships will be an indication of their spirituality.

The deepest pain a person can suffer is the pain caused by the uncharitable wound of someone we love. The persecution caused by the world outside is one thing, but the hostility and hatred of a friend or a family member is more demanding and more difficult. The word Matthew uses for hate in verse 22 is MISEO. It means deep-seated abhorrence and hostility towards an other.

How should the disciples respond to such hatred? What is the appropriate response to such overt animosity? Jesus tells us “But he who stands firm shall be saved.” We could very easily misunderstand what Jesus is saying here. When we think of standing firm we think in terms of clenching your fist, gritting your teeth, being strong and just endure what comes. But this is not what Jesus is saying.

There are three important things we need to notice about the word “Stand firm”

The word stand firm is the Greek word HYPOMENO, which is also translated patient, persevere, endure, be steadfast. The word means to hold your ground, and was used to describe a soldier staying in the heat of the battle under terrible opposition. It was also used of a proud Greek, who was a free man without responsibilities, but who chooses to endure a burden, difficulty or danger without any hope of reward.

The word was used as a Christian virtue e.g. it was used as a means of expressing love 1 Cor. 13:7

Love, always protects, always trusts, always hopes, and always perseveres.1 Cor. 13:7

It is an expression of Joy Hebrews 12:2-3 ‘Let us fix our eyes on Jesus, the author and perfecter of our faith, who for the joy set before him endured the cross, scorning its shame, and sat down at the right hand of the throne of God. Consider him who endured such opposition from sinful men, so that you will not grow weary and lose heart.’

It is also an expression of Hope

Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer; Romans 12:12

So what are we saying?

The only way we can cope with undeserved hostility, the only way we can stand firm and hold our ground, is to ensure that our endurance is motivated by love joy and hope. Endurance which is a sole expression of self determination will not last.

The most important thing about handling hostility, is how we handle ourselves, we will not be able to handle hostility until we learn the value of self-control and how we should handle ourselves.

There is a third thing about this word that is extremely important. Jesus said, “But he who stand firm to the end will be saved.” The word HYPOMENO also means to remain under. One Greek scholar defines hypomeno as “to remain under a trial in a God honouring way as to learn the lessons they are sent to teach rather than attempt get our from under them, in an effort to be relieved from their pressure.” Those who endure, those who find God’s purpose through the hostility will be saved. They will not crumble under the pressure. When Jesus speaks about being saved here he is not talking about the salvation of our souls, but about dealing with the hostility without loosing you commitment to God and his kingdom.

It is interesting to note that more people loose their faith, of leave Christina work, not because of difficult circumstances, but because the pain of difficult relationships.

When Jesus says “but he who stands firm to the end will be saved.” He is saying that if we allow bitterness or anger or resentment to take hold in our hearts, then there is no way we will survive thee hostility of others. If our standing firm is not a reflection of faith hope or love, then we will become bitter and angry. You could say that only those who have a robust godly character have the ability to ‘stand firm.’
prayer: Father help me to have a character that endures.
